newsitem.title: USA: US Justice okays American Radio/EZ Comm merger.
newsitem.headline: US Justice okays American Radio/EZ Comm merger.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department said Thursday it would allow Boston-based American Radio Systems Corp to go forward with its $655 million merger with EZ Communications Inc.
The department's antitrust division said it allowed the deal as long as American Radio divested one radio station in Sacramento, California, and another one in Charlotte, North Carolina.
After the divestiture, American Radio will own seven radio stations in the Charlotte area, accounting for about 40 percent of the radio advertising revenues, department officials said.
In Sacramento, after the sale, American Radio will own seven stations in the area, accounting for about 33 percent of the radio advertising revenues, they said.

The Justice Department said it filed two civil suits claiming that the original deal would lessen competition in the two cities, and a proposed settlement resolving the lawsuits as a result of the divestitures of the two stations.

The department said American Radio owns 75 stations in 14 metropolitan areas in the United States and had 1996 revenues of about $270 million while EZ owns 23 stations in seven cities and had revenues of $118 million last year.
